title: Solution structure of the Z0 domain from transcription repressor BCL11A sheds light on the sequence properties of protein-binding zinc-fingers
authors: Rilee E. Harris; Richard D. Whitehead; Andrei T. Alexandrescu
one_liner_zh: 该文通过NMR解析BCL11A Z0结构并分析锌指序列特征以区分DNA结合与非结合锌指，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作但无AI/物理模拟方法，仅序列统计，故为中档。
abstract: The transcription repressor BCL11A, which governs the switch from fetal to adult hemoglobin during development, is the target of the first FDA-approved CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing therapy in humans. By targeting BCL11A, fetal hemoglobin expression is de-repressed to substitute for defective adult hemoglobin in inherited diseases including beta-thalassemia and sickle-cell anemia. BCL11A has six CCHH-type zinc-fingers of which domains 4-6 are necessary and sufficient for dsDNA binding. Here, we focus on the CCHC-type ZNF at the N-terminus of BCL11A (residues 46-72), Z0, thought to modulate oligomerization of the transcription repressor. Using NMR and CD spectroscopy, Z0 is shown to be a thermostable CCHC zinc-finger with a pM dissociation constant for zinc. The NMR structure of Z0 has a prototypical beta-beta-alpha fold, with a hydrophobic knob comprising about half the structure. The unusual proportion of hydrophobic residues in Z0 led us to investigate if this is more general in zinc-fingers that do not bind dsDNA. We used the ZF and WebLogo servers to examine sequences of zinc fingers with demonstrated DNA-binding function, non-binders, and the CCHC-type family of protein-binders. DNA-binders are distinguished by contiguous stretches of high-scoring zinc-fingers. Non-DNA-binders show a depletion of polar residues at the positions expected to contact nucleotides and increased divergence from sequence consensus making these domains more likely to be annotated as atypical, degenerate, or to be missed as zinc-fingers. We anticipate these sequence patterns will help distinguish DNA-binders from non-binders, an open problem in the functional understanding of zinc-finger motifs.
abstract_zh: 转录抑制因子BCL11A在发育过程中调控胎儿血红蛋白向成人血红蛋白的转换，是首个获FDA批准的CRISPR/Cas9基因编辑疗法在人类中的靶点。通过靶向BCL11A，胎儿血红蛋白的表达被去抑制，以替代遗传性疾病（包括β-地中海贫血和镰状细胞性贫血）中有缺陷的成人血红蛋白。BCL11A含有六个CCHH型锌指，其中结构域4-6对于双链DNA（dsDNA）结合是必要且充分的。在此，我们聚焦于BCL11A N端的CCHC型锌指（残基46-72），即Z0，该结构域被认为调节转录抑制因子的寡聚化。利用核磁共振（NMR）和圆二色（CD）光谱，Z0被证明是一种热稳定的CCHC锌指，其对锌的解离常数为pM级。Z0的NMR结构具有典型的β-β-α折叠，其中包含一个约占结构一半的疏水凸起。Z0中异常高的疏水残基比例促使我们探究这一特征是否在非dsDNA结合的锌指中更为普遍。我们使用ZF和WebLogo服务器检查了具有明确DNA结合功能的锌指、非结合者以及CCHC型蛋白结合家族的序列。DNA结合者以连续的高评分锌指片段为特征。非DNA结合者在预期接触核苷酸的位置显示出极性残基的减少，并且与序列共识的差异增加，使得这些结构域更可能被注释为非典型、退化型，或被遗漏为锌指。我们预期这些序列模式将有助于区分DNA结合者与非结合者，这是锌指基序功能理解中的一个开放问题。
